$comment: Schema for the collections the notification bell reads and the notifications service writes. Nothing applies this file for you: create the collections and fields with your backend's own tools (the DaaS MCP / Studio), then create EVERY foreign key with a relation call. Rows are written only by the notifications service (elevated); people read their own rows and may only set read_at.

collections.note: One row per notification. recipient is a user; recipient_email (lower-case) is for a person without an account, who gets the digest email only.

fields.note: The user notified. Null when recipient_email is used.
Lower-case address of a person without an account (digest only).
The record it is about (checked by the optional visibility hook)
At most one row per key; the service tolerates the unique violation (23505) of a concurrent insert.
Set by the bell. The only field people may update.
Set when emailed (immediate or digest) or handled by the digest.
Set by the service; bumped when a row is merged.

indexes.note: The bell's list and unread count

collections.note: Optional. One row per person who changed the default. No row: email_mode immediate.

create.note: A create hook stamps user = the caller

services: ./services/notifications.js, as a custom service named notifications
hooks: ./hooks/*.hook.js: mention and reply (on <comments>.items.create), assign (on <collection>.items.update), and the optional visibility filter (on notifications.items.read)
